The U.S. has deployed two warships to the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea. The freedom-of-navigation operation follows a collision between two Chinese vessels that were aggressively blocking a Philippine coast guard ship.
https://t.co/vB4e7PI16f
 US Briefly Deploys 2 Warships to a Disputed South China Sea Shoal After Chinese Collision

The U.S. deployed two warships Wednesday in a disputed South China Sea shoal where two Chinese ships collided earlier in the week while trying to drive away a smaller Philippine ship in a high-seas accident that raised alarms about maritime safety.

Both China and the Philippines claim Scarborough Shoal and other outcroppings in the South China Sea. Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan also lay overlapping claims in the contested waters.

The USS Higgins, a guided missile destroyer, and USS Cincinnati, a littoral combat ship, were shadowed by a Chinese navy ship while sailing about 30 nautical miles (55 kilometers) from the Scarborough Shoal. There were no reports of any untoward incident, Philippine coast guard Commodore Jay Tarriela said, citing information from U.S. officials and a Philippine surveillance flight.

The U.S. Navy has staged what it calls freedom-of-navigation voyages and overflights in the South China Sea for years to challenge China’s restrictions and its demand for entry notifications in virtually the entire stretch of the disputed waters that it claims. That has angered China and its forces have had close runs-in with U.S. warships and aircraft on such patrols in international waters and airspace.

The deployment happened after Washington’s ambassador to Manila, MaryKay Carlson, on Tuesday condemned “the latest reckless action by China directed against a Philippine vessel” in Scarborough. The rich fishing atoll off the northwestern Philippines has been the scene of increasingly tense confrontations between the Chinese and Philippine coast guard, fishing and other ships in recent years.

The Philippines is the oldest treaty ally of the U.S. in Asia. Washington has repeatedly warned that it’s obligated to defend the Philippines if Filipino forces come under an armed attack, including in the South China Sea.

On Monday, a Chinese navy destroyer and a Chinese coast guard ship accidentally collided while trying to block and drive away a smaller Philippine coast guard ship, the BRP Suluan, about 10.5 nautical miles (19 kilometers) from Scarborough. Video footages made public by the Philippine coast guard show the Chinese coast guard ship blasting its powerful water cannon and a number of Chinese personnel standing at the bow shortly before that section was hit by the fast-turning Chinese navy ship.

Shortly after the collision, the video shows the heavily shattered bow of the Chinese coast guard ship without the Chinese personnel, who were standing on deck before the crash. The Chinese navy ship sustained deep dents and what appeared to be linear gushes on its hull.

Japan, Australia and New Zealand expressed alarm on Wednesday over the dangerous maneuvers that led to the collision in the busy waters, a key global trade route.

“Japan upholds the rule of law and opposes any actions which increase tensions. Our concern goes to the repeated actions in the South China Sea,” Japanese Ambassador to Manila Endo Kazuya said in a post on X.

The Australian Embassy in Manila expressed concern “by the dangerous and unprofessional conduct of Chinese vessels near Scarborough Shoal involving the Philippine Coast Guard,” saying in a statement the incident “highlights the need for de-escalation, restraint and respect for international law.”

“This is a learning experience for the People’s Republic of China,” Tarriela, the Philippine coast guard commodore, told a news conference in Manila. “For so many years, we have been reminding them to stop dangerous maneuvers, to stop risky blockings, to adhere to the (anti-)collision regulations because if there is a very high chance of miscalculation, this kind of collision incident would happen.”

Tarriela spoke a few hours after a Chinese fighter jet flew as close as 500 feet (150 meters) to try to drive away a Philippine coast guard plane on a surveillance flight on Wednesday over the Scarborough with invited journalists on board. The Chinese jet carried out dangerous maneuvers for about 20 minutes, including flying about 200 feet (60 meters) above the small Philippine aircraft, Tarriela said.

🇮🇳 India's Economic Landscape: A Sector-by-Sector Breakdown with Fastest Growing Sectors #MakeInIndia

💫Renewable Energy:

1st - 🇨🇳 China
2nd - 🇺🇸 United States
3rd - 🇮🇳 India (India also ranks 4th globally in installed Renewable Energy Capacity and 4th in Wind Power.)
4th - 🇯🇵 Japan
5th - 🇩🇪 Germany

💫Technology and IT:

Top outsourcing countries (ranking varies depending on the specific criteria, but these are consistently mentioned):
🇨🇳 China
🇮🇳 India
🇵🇱 Poland
🇷🇴 Romania
🇵🇭 Philippines

💫Pharmaceuticals & Healthcare:

India is the 3rd largest producer of medicines globally by volume.
India supplies over 50% of global vaccine demand.

Top 5 global pharmaceutical companies by revenue (among the top 10):
🇺🇸 Pfizer
🇨🇭 Roche
🇺🇸 Johnson & Johnson
🇨🇭 Novartis
🇺🇸 Merck & Co.

💫Automotive (with a focus on EVs):
1st - 🇨🇳 China
2nd - 🇺🇸 United States
3rd - 🇮🇳 India
4th - 🇯🇵 Japan
5th - 🇰🇷 South Korea

💫Financial Services (especially Fintech):
1st - 🇺🇸 United States
2nd - 🇬🇧 United Kingdom
3rd - 🇮🇳 India
4th - 🇨🇦 Canada
5th - 🇧🇷 Brazil 
Sectors with Notable Contributions

💫Agriculture:

Top 5 Agricultural Producers by volume (ranking may vary slightly depending on the specific agricultural products included in the measurement):
🇨🇳 China
🇺🇸 United States
🇧🇷 Brazil
🇮🇳 India
🇷🇺 Russia

👉Top 5 Wheat Producing Countries in 2025:
1st - 🇨🇳 China
2nd - 🇮🇳 India
3rd - 🇷🇺 Russia
4th - 🇺🇸 United States
5th - 🇦🇺 Australia

India ranks 8th globally in agricultural exports.

United States 🇺🇸: The US is projected to maintain its position as a leading exporter in terms of value, with a strong focus on commodities like soybeans, corn, and beef.

Brazil 🇧🇷: Brazil continues to be a major player, particularly in the export of soybeans, coffee, and beef.
Netherlands 

🇳🇱: Despite its relatively small size, the Netherlands consistently ranks high due to its expertise in exporting flowers, dairy products, and high-value vegetables.

China 🇨🇳: While a significant agricultural importer, China is also a notable exporter of products like aquatic goods, fruits, and vegetables.

India 🇮🇳: India ranks 8th among the top agricultural exporters, particularly in rice (including Basmati), spices, and tea. 

💫FMCG and Consumer Durables: 

India is the 4th largest sector in the economy, projected for significant growth.

💫Infrastructure and Construction: 

India's construction sector is projected to be the third largest globally by 2025.

💫 Metals and Mining: 

India is the 2nd largest producer of crude steel and aluminum. 

China 🇨🇳: China continues to be the largest crude steel producer.

India 🇮🇳: India maintains its position as the second largest crude steel producer.

Japan 🇯🇵: Japan is the third largest producer.

United States 🇺🇸: The US holds the fourth position.

Russia 🇷🇺: Russia is the fifth largest crude steel producer. 

💫 Defense and Aerospace: 

India ranks 4th globally in military strength in the Global Firepower 2025 Index. India is also the 5th highest military spender globally.

Top 5 Military Spenders (by budget):
1st - 🇺🇸 United States
2nd - 🇨🇳 China
3rd - 🇷🇺 Russia
4th - 🇩🇪 Germany
5th - 🇮🇳 India 

Note: Rankings can fluctuate depending on the specific methodology and the exact year of analysis. The data presented here is latest as of 2025 & it's based on my studies

TRAFFIC ADVISORY

IN CONNECTION WITH WALKATHON UNDER HAR GHAR TIRANGA CAMPAIGN ON 14.08.25 AT 09:00 HOURS

A Walkathon will be held by Directorate of Education, GNCTD on 14.08.2025 from 0900 hours at Shakti Nagar, Delhi.
Due to the walkathon, traffic will remain affected on Vyas Marg, Lacchmandas Aggarwal Marg, GT Karnal Road crossing Shakti Nagar, Laxmi Narayan Marg, Inder Chandra Shastri Marg on 14.08.2025 from 09:00 AM onwards for general road users except emergency vehicles.

DIVERSION POINTS: -

Shakti Nagar Chowk Red Light
Nagia Park.
Swami Narayan- Inder Chander Shastri Marg Red Light

All vehicles will be diverted from the above points as and when required.

ALTERNATE ROUTE:-

Traffic coming from Nanak Piao on GT Karnal Road :-
The traffic destined to Shakti Nagar Chowk Red Light from Nanak Piao will be diverted to Bhama Shah Marg and then take Sant Kirpal Singh Marg to reach their destinations.
Traffic coming from Ghanta Ghar on GT Karnal Road :-
The traffic destined to Nanak Piao from Ghanta Ghar Shakti Nagar will be diverted from Shakti Nagar Chowk to Satyawati Marg and then take Sant Kirpal Singh Marg to reach their destinations.
Traffic coming from P.S Roop Nagar on Inder Chandra Shastri Marg:-
The traffic destined to Nagia Park from Roop Nagar will be diverted from Shakti Nagar Chowk to GT Karnal Road and then take Roshanara Road to reach their destinations.
Traffic coming from P.S Roop Nagar on Inder Chandra Shastri Marg:-
The traffic destined to Nagia Park from Roop Nagar will be diverted from Shakti Nagar Chowk to GT Karnal Road and then take Roshanara Road to reach their destinations
Traffic coming from Swami Narayan Marg on Inder Chandra Shastri Marg:-
The traffic destined to Nagia Park from Swami Narayan Marg will be diverted from Swami Narayan- Inder Chander Shastri Marg Red Light to  Swami Narayan Marg (straight) and then take Swami Narayan Underpass road-Bhama Shah Marg-Sant Kirpal Singh Marg to reach their destinations.

INSTRUCTIONS TO GENERAL PUBLIC: -

-Commuters are advised to avoid the above roads.

-Avoid roadside parking as it causes hindrance to normal flow of traffic.
